summary: Official warnings state that health conditions which make urine less acidic can slow down how the body clears Memantine Hydrochloride, leading to higher amounts of the medicine building up in the blood [3]. In addition, a small computer model rather than testing on people estimated that the risk scores for both the liver and the heart are in the low range [M]. Several clinical studies were stopped early for non-safety reasons, including slow recruitment coupled with drug expiration, loss of funding and staff, and a trial failing to show a meaningful benefit compared to an inactive dummy pill [5][6][7].
